name: sheet
title: Sheet
description: A modal panel that slides in from an edge of the viewport, for filters, details and secondary tasks that keep the page in context.

examples.name: sheet-demo
examples.title: Filters panel
examples.description: Fields in a scrollable body with actions pinned to the bottom.

examples.name: sheet-sides
examples.title: Sides
examples.description: start, end, top and bottom. start and end are logical and swap in right-to-left layouts.

props.name: side
props.description: Edge the panel is attached to. end is the right edge in LTR and the left edge in RTL.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading; also the panel's accessible name.

props.name: children
props.description: Panel content; scrolls independently of the header and footer.

props.name: footer
props.description: Actions pinned to the bottom of the panel.

props.name: isDismissable
props.description: Whether clicking the backdrop closes the sheet.

props.name: isOpen / defaultOpen / onOpenChange
props.description: Open state when not inside a DialogTrigger.

props.name: className / style
props.description: Applied to the panel, e.g. to change its width.

keyboard.action: On the trigger: opens the sheet and moves focus into it.
Moves between focusable elements; focus is trapped inside the sheet.
Closes the sheet and returns focus to the trigger.

notes: A modal dialog (role="dialog") named by its title; the page behind is inert while it is open.

Overlays render in a portal on <body>, outside any ThemeScope. When it opens, the overlay copies data-strata-theme, data-strata-scheme and data-strata-density from the nearest [data-strata-theme] ancestor of its trigger (or of where the component is rendered, when controlled), plus dir and lang, onto its own root — so it uses the same tenant tokens and direction as the page region it came from, and nested overlays inherit from their parent overlay.
Right-to-left: set dir on the scope for layout, and wrap the app in React Aria's I18nProvider with an RTL locale so keyboard arrows and start/end placement flip too.

do: Use end for detail and filter panels, bottom for short mobile actions.
Keep the primary action in the footer so it stays visible while the body scrolls.
dont: Don't use a sheet for navigation that should stay visible — use a persistent sidebar.
